categories.name: Picks the Right Brain for the Job
categories.description: Monolithic cloud models are slow, expensive, and leak secrets. Tiny local models choke on complex tasks. Halbert routes every turn to the right endpoint.

categories.name: Knows What's Wrong Before You Do
categories.description: Machines fail silently; traditional monitoring buries signal in noise. Halbert probes, detects, and explains — before it becomes your problem.

categories.name: Safe Surgery on System Files
categories.description: One bad edit in /etc can brick a machine. Halbert previews impact, proposes diffs, rolls back on failure, and remembers why you made every change.

categories.name: Answers Grounded in Real Documentation
categories.description: LLMs invent nonexistent flags and dangerous shell arguments. Halbert searches 14,000 verified manuals before answering.

categories.name: A Workspace, Not Another Chat Window
categories.description: Juggling a chatbot, terminal, and monitoring app in separate windows creates constant friction. Halbert is one integrated environment.

categories.name: Speaks and Listens Without the Cloud
categories.description: Cloud voice assistants lag, fail offline, and can't detect a smoke alarm at 2 AM. Halbert's entire sensory pipeline runs on your hardware.

categories.name: One Mind Across Every Machine
categories.description: Managing a fleet of servers and devices means juggling SSH sessions and separate credentials. Halbert federates them under one identity.

categories.name: A Home That Pays Attention
categories.description: Smart-home hubs automate schedules but don't notice anomalies or reason about occupancy. Halbert bridges the gap between automation and awareness.

features.name: Right-Sized Intelligence
features.category: Picks the Right Brain for the Job
features.oneLine: Automatically routes simple queries to fast local models and reserves deep reasoning for complex system diffs.
features.whatItIs: Halbert does not route every turn to a single monolithic cloud model. It maintains dedicated tiers — Guide (fast conversational triage), Specialist (complex sysadmin synthesis and code diffing), and Vision (image and diagram analysis) — each backed by independently configurable endpoints.
features.howItWorks: Incoming messages are scored for intent and complexity by the intake pipeline. The TierRouter checks available hardware capabilities and configuration before selecting the optimal endpoint. Debug mode surfaces the routing decision for every turn so you can see exactly why a query went where it did.
features.limitsAndInvariants: If a configured endpoint goes down, routing gracefully degrades to the next available tier rather than failing silently.

features.name: Air-Gapped Private Execution
features.category: Picks the Right Brain for the Job
features.oneLine: Sensitive credentials and system configs never egress to cloud APIs. Fail-closed, not fail-open.
features.whatItIs: A safety boundary that prevents queries involving SSH keys, firewall rules, or private configuration files from ever being evaluated by remote third-party cloud endpoints. When sensitive context is detected, the agent latches to strictly local inference.
features.howItWorks: The secure context evaluator in the agent state machine detects sensitive tokens and system file paths. When triggered, execution locks to local loopback endpoints (Ollama, Metal, vLLM). If no local model is available, the turn halts and informs the user rather than silently downgrading to a cloud model.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Fails closed: absence of a local model means the query is refused, never silently sent to the cloud.

features.name: Hot-Swap Any Provider
features.category: Picks the Right Brain for the Job
features.oneLine: Switch between Ollama, LM Studio, Apple Foundation Models, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Azure without restarting.
features.whatItIs: A headless model picker package that renders provider cards, discovers local models, and lets you assign any discovered model to any tier slot — all without restarting the daemon or losing conversation context.
features.howItWorks: The @halbert/model-picker package is fully headless: zero I/O, zero hardcoded class names. It defines a ModelPickerTransport interface that the host implements. Endpoint discovery probes each configured provider's API for available models. The picker supports 8 provider types: Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Google, Azure OpenAI, and Apple Foundation.
features.limitsAndInvariants: The picker never performs fetch calls directly — all I/O goes through the injected transport, so it works identically in tests, Tauri IPC, and REST contexts.

features.name: Context Window Compression
features.category: Picks the Right Brain for the Job
features.oneLine: Level-of-Detail memory management keeping long conversations from blowing the context ceiling.
features.whatItIs: As conversations grow, raw token counts can exceed the model's context window. The compression subsystem applies lingua and semantic compressors to distill earlier turns into denser representations while preserving critical facts and tool outputs.
features.howItWorks: The lingua compressor removes syntactic filler and redundancy. The semantic compressor identifies and merges duplicate information across turns. Together they maintain a sliding window of full-fidelity recent turns backed by compressed summaries of older context.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Compression never discards tool outputs or system-state observations — only conversational filler and redundant explanations are candidates for reduction.

features.name: Structured Agent Lifecycle
features.category: Picks the Right Brain for the Job
features.oneLine: Every turn moves through formal states with strict tool-call budgets and CRAG verification.
features.whatItIs: The cognitive lifecycle engine that orchestrates turns through a deterministic finite state machine: IDLE → PLANNING → SEARCHING → READING → EXECUTING → OBSERVING → REFLECTING → RESPONDING. Each state transition is logged and auditable.
features.howItWorks: In PLANNING, the model selects tools. In EXECUTING, tools are validated against policy and invoked. In OBSERVING, CRAG (Corrective RAG) checks verify tool outputs and classify them as CORRECT, INCORRECT, or AMBIGUOUS before generating the user response. Tool call quotas and execution timeouts prevent infinite loops.
features.limitsAndInvariants: No infinite tool loops: each turn enforces strict tool call quotas and execution timeouts. CRAG evaluation gates every tool output before it reaches the response.

features.name: Secure Credential Storage
features.category: Picks the Right Brain for the Job
features.oneLine: Encrypted vault for API keys and provider secrets — never stored in plaintext config files.
features.whatItIs: Provider API keys, Home Assistant tokens, and other secrets are stored in an encrypted credential vault rather than plaintext YAML. The vault is keyed to the local machine identity.
features.howItWorks: The crypto storage module handles encryption at rest, key derivation, and secure retrieval. Secrets are never logged, never included in debug output, and never transmitted to the model as part of conversation context.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Keys are never rendered in debug logs or included in model prompts. The picker UI masks API keys in the provider card display.

features.name: 37 Pluggable System Scanners
features.category: Knows What's Wrong Before You Do
features.oneLine: Live probing across Linux and macOS: disks, SMART, thermal, USB, network, services, packages, wifi, boot, display, containers, processes, and more.
features.whatItIs: An extensible discovery engine that inspects every measurable dimension of a running system. 24 core scanners cover storage, services, network, security, sharing, backups, thermal, GPU, USB, display, containers, processes, boot, and more. 3 app scanners handle Flatpak, Snap, and AppImage. 10 macOS-specific scanners cover Homebrew, launchd, Time Machine, Mac App Store, and platform-native network/security/sharing/storage/thermal interfaces.
features.howItWorks: Scanners run concurrently under an execution budget, parsing native OS data (sysfs, procfs, systemctl, ioreg, system_profiler) into strongly-typed Discovery records. Results feed both the dashboard pages and the agent's contextual awareness.
features.toolingAndBackend: discovery/engine.py, discovery/scanners/ (24 files), discovery/scanners/apps/ (3 files), discovery/scanners/macos/ (10 files)
features.limitsAndInvariants: Read-only non-destructive operations: discovery scanners never mutate system state or modify filesystem configuration.

features.name: GPU & AI Accelerator Diagnostics
features.category: Knows What's Wrong Before You Do
features.oneLine: Dedicated hardware inspection for GPUs (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Metal) and AI accelerators (Coral TPU, Hailo, MemryX, NPUs).
features.whatItIs: Specialized deep inspection for compute hardware that goes beyond basic discovery. Detects GPU architecture, driver versions, VRAM allocation, thermal state, and active workloads. For AI accelerators, identifies attached edge TPUs and neural processing units with their firmware and runtime status.
features.howItWorks: GPU tools probe nvidia-smi, rocm-smi, intel_gpu_top, and Metal system profiler. Accelerator tools detect Coral Edge TPUs, Hailo-8/8L/10H, MemryX MX3, Intel NPU, AMD XDNA NPU, and Apple Neural Engine through platform-specific APIs and device enumeration.
features.limitsAndInvariants: GPU analysis is cached to YAML with a 7-day TTL to avoid redundant expensive probes.

features.name: The Four Whys
features.category: Knows What's Wrong Before You Do
features.oneLine: Every finding explains why now, why care, why so, and why trust — with real detector evidence, not raw error dumps.
features.whatItIs: Replaces raw discovery alerts with curated Findings. Before Halbert interrupts you, it must justify why the issue matters right now, why you should care, what evidence supports the claim, and why the detection is trustworthy. The FindingStore persists these records with full provenance.
features.howItWorks: Detector sweeps (acoustic anomaly detection, permissions hygiene checks, and more) aggregate low-level scanner anomalies. When an anomaly breaches thresholds, a Finding record is generated with four justification fields and queued in the attention ledger. Dashboard routes expose the findings list and allow proposing fixes.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Zero vanity notifications: findings respect user-defined quiet hours and the proactivity dial.

features.name: Calm Notification Attunement
features.category: Knows What's Wrong Before You Do
features.oneLine: Push (voice, auto-open panels), Ambient (badges, tray indicator), Pull (findings page, timeline) — three attention tiers.
features.whatItIs: A surface taxonomy that classifies every way Halbert can reach a person by its attention cost. Push surfaces (voice, satellite audio, panel auto-open) arrive unbidden and spend attention — they're suppressed during withdrawal periods. Ambient surfaces (bell badge, presence pill, tray indicator) change without being asked but demand nothing. Pull surfaces (findings page, events API, timeline) persist for the user to navigate to and are never suppressed.
features.howItWorks: Each of Halbert's 9 output surfaces is classified as PUSH, AMBIENT, or PULL. The attunement sensor tracks the user's engagement state, and the shadow module manages withdrawal — silencing push surfaces while preserving ambient indicators and never hiding pull content.
features.limitsAndInvariants: A withdrawal must silence the voice and auto-opening panels but must never hide a findings row or empty the bell — suppressing a surface the user navigates to destroys information they asked to find.

features.name: Autonomous Self-Management Cycles
features.category: Knows What's Wrong Before You Do
features.oneLine: 5-phase background loops (Sense → Deliberate → Propose → Act → Reflect) driving autonomous issue resolution.
features.whatItIs: A somatic block is the wrapper that drives a single self-management cycle through five phases. It references — but does not absorb — the existing Finding, Proposal, ApprovalRequest, Action, and Reflection models by ID, composing them into a complete autonomous resolution arc.
features.howItWorks: The SomaticLifecycle orchestrator drives each block through its phases: SENSORY gathers scanner data, DELIBERATION evaluates severity and blast radius, PROPOSAL generates a config change through the ProposalGenerator, ACTION executes through the approval engine (if approved), and REFLECTION logs the outcome and adjusts future detection thresholds.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Every action phase routes through the approval engine — somatic blocks cannot bypass human-in-the-loop authorization for state-mutating operations.

features.name: Proactive Morning Reports & Reflexes
features.category: Knows What's Wrong Before You Do
features.oneLine: Autonomous daily briefing and reflexive responses to significant events without waiting for user prompting.
features.whatItIs: The proactive subsystem generates a structured morning report summarizing overnight findings, scanner anomalies, and pending approval requests. Reflexes respond to significant events (security alerts, hardware failures, acoustic anomalies) in near-real-time without requiring the user to ask.
features.howItWorks: The morning report aggregates overnight findings, scanner deltas, and pending items into a briefing. Reflexes subscribe to event streams and trigger the agent when predefined conditions are met. The acoustic bridge connects audio pipeline anomaly detections to the reflex system.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Reflexes respect the attunement withdrawal state — they will not interrupt during withdrawal periods unless the event is classified as critical.

features.name: Full Computer Vision Suite
features.category: Knows What's Wrong Before You Do
features.oneLine: Screen capture (Wayland-aware), ambient webcam monitoring, OCR text extraction, and motion detection.
features.whatItIs: A comprehensive local vision subsystem that extends far beyond simple image pasting. Screen capture works on both X11 and Wayland compositors. Ambient webcam monitoring detects environmental changes. OCR extracts text from screenshots and documents. Motion detection identifies physical movement in camera feeds.
features.howItWorks: Each vision module operates independently with graceful degradation — if onnxruntime is not installed, the pipeline starts but produces no observations (no crash). Screen capture uses platform-specific APIs (Wayland portal, X11 capture, macOS screencapturekit). OCR runs locally via Tesseract or ONNX models.
features.limitsAndInvariants: All vision processing is strictly local — no images are ever transmitted to cloud services unless the user explicitly configures a cloud vision model.

features.name: Apps & Container Management
features.category: Knows What's Wrong Before You Do
features.oneLine: Docker, Podman, Flatpak, Snap, and AppImage lifecycle management with a dedicated dashboard panel.
features.whatItIs: A dedicated dashboard panel for managing containerized and packaged applications. Scans for running Docker and Podman containers, installed Flatpak apps and remotes, Snap packages and channels, and AppImage files. Provides inspection, status monitoring, and lifecycle controls.
features.howItWorks: The container scanner probes Docker and Podman sockets for running containers, images, and resource usage. App scanners enumerate installed Flatpak, Snap, and AppImage applications. The dashboard routes expose these through REST APIs consumed by the frontend panel.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Container lifecycle operations (start, stop, remove) require approval for destructive actions.

features.name: Blast Radius Before You Edit
features.category: Safe Surgery on System Files
features.oneLine: Config dependency graph showing exactly which services break if you change a file, before you touch it.
features.whatItIs: Before modifying any system configuration file, Halbert can calculate its blast radius — the set of services, mount points, and other config files that directly depend on it. This turns a blind edit into an informed decision.
features.howItWorks: The ConfigEdgeExtractor builds a dependency graph by parsing systemd unit dependencies, config file Include/Import directives, fstab device-to-mountpoint mappings, and absolute-path file references. The BlastRadiusCalculator traverses this graph to return shallow (direct) dependents for any given config path.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Currently returns shallow (direct) dependents only — deep transitive traversal is a future enhancement.

features.name: AI Diff Proposals with Instant Rollback
features.category: Safe Surgery on System Files
features.oneLine: SEARCH/REPLACE proposals rendered as visual diffs in Monaco, with mandatory pre-save snapshots and one-click restore.
features.whatItIs: Halbert generates structured SEARCH/REPLACE edit blocks for system configuration files. The Monaco editor renders a visual side-by-side diff so you see exactly what will change. Applying a change automatically creates a timestamped .bak backup. If anything goes wrong, the editor route provides a one-click /backup/restore endpoint.
features.howItWorks: The WriteConfig tool generates unified diffs for proposed changes, saves a .bak copy before modification, and supports a do_rollback flag to immediately restore from backup. The editor API route adds full backup listing and restore capabilities on top.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Atomic file writing: failures abort cleanly without leaving partial or corrupted configuration on disk.

features.name: Intent Kept Next to the Change
features.category: Safe Surgery on System Files
features.oneLine: The "Why Brain" captures the human rationale alongside config changes and restores it into future conversation context.
features.whatItIs: You moved SSH to port 2222 on July 14th because the auth log was filling with scans. Halbert keeps the reason beside the change, with the evidence, so six months from now neither of you has to guess. The Why Brain UI is a clickable brain icon on discovery pages (GPU, Services, Storage, Containers, Network).
features.howItWorks: Clicking the brain icon records or shows a user-authored explanation for why an item is configured a certain way. Rationales are served by get_self_knowledge() and injected into future chat context, so the agent remembers your reasoning when you ask about that configuration again.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Rationales are user-curated, never auto-generated — the agent may suggest a reason, but the user confirms it.

features.name: Cross-Session Memory Vault
features.category: Safe Surgery on System Files
features.oneLine: Threads, receipts, and machine-state history survive reboots without polluting active prompts with stale context.
features.whatItIs: Halbert's cross-session continuity system preserves conversation threads, tool execution receipts, and machine-state ledger entries across reboots. The VaultProjector reconciles the internal change ledger into human-readable Markdown notes that you can browse and edit on disk.
features.howItWorks: The StateStore maintains a ledger of machine-state triples (subject, predicate, value) with timestamps and actor attribution. The Consolidator merges redundant entries at idle time. The VaultProjector exports the ledger into a vault directory of plain Markdown files, maintaining byte-identity and unlinking orphans during rebuilds.
features.limitsAndInvariants: The vault projection has no authority — it is a human-readable view, not the source of truth. The StateStore ledger is canonical.

features.name: Change Provenance Tracking
features.category: Safe Surgery on System Files
features.oneLine: Who changed a file, when, and why — linked to the state ledger with actor, reason, and content digest.
features.whatItIs: Every configuration file modification made through Halbert is recorded with full provenance: which actor (user or system) made the change, the reason given, a content digest of the file before and after, and a timestamp. This creates a complete audit trail.
features.howItWorks: The provenance module hooks into the WriteConfig tool and records file mode changes, content modifications, and actor attributions. Each record links back to the state ledger and can be queried to reconstruct the complete history of a file.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Provenance records are append-only — they cannot be retroactively modified or deleted.

features.name: Human-in-the-Loop Approval Queue
features.category: Safe Surgery on System Files
features.oneLine: Mandatory user authorization gate for state-mutating actions with a dedicated dashboard page.
features.whatItIs: Every destructive or state-mutating action the agent proposes — config writes, service restarts, package installations — must pass through the approval queue. The dashboard's Approvals page displays pending requests with exact proposed commands and affected paths.
features.howItWorks: The ApprovalEngine receives tool call requests, creates ApprovalRequest records (PENDING), and routes them to the dashboard. The Approvals page polls for pending requests and lets the user approve or reject with a reason. Approved actions execute through the standard tool pipeline; rejected actions are recorded with the rejection reason.
features.limitsAndInvariants: AI Rules filter conflicting approvals. The approval engine never auto-approves — user interaction is always required for state-mutating operations.

features.name: Pre-Execution Dry-Run Simulation
features.category: Safe Surgery on System Files
features.oneLine: Simulates file writes, service restarts, and tool calls before touching disk — preview the impact without the risk.
features.whatItIs: The simulation engine lets you preview the effects of a proposed action before committing. File writes show the resulting file content, service restarts show dependent services that would be affected, and command simulations show expected output patterns.
features.howItWorks: API endpoints (/api/settings/simulate/file-write, /command, /service-restart, /tool) evaluate proposed actions against safety guardrails and the blast radius calculator, producing an impact report without executing mutations.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Backend implementation is complete; no dedicated frontend visualizer exists yet — simulation results are currently only accessible via API.

features.name: Offline Hybrid Retrieval
features.category: Answers Grounded in Real Documentation
features.oneLine: Sparse BM25 keyword matching merged with dense semantic embeddings via Reciprocal Rank Fusion — no cloud search needed.
features.whatItIs: Halbert's knowledge retrieval combines two complementary search strategies. BM25 sparse retrieval excels at exact keyword matches (specific flag names, error codes). Dense embedding retrieval finds semantically similar content even when the exact words differ. Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges both result sets, and optional cross-encoder reranking provides final precision.
features.howItWorks: Queries are dispatched concurrently to BM25 and dense vector indices. Results are merged using RRF scoring. The top candidates are optionally reranked by a cross-encoder for maximum precision before being injected into the agent's prompt context.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Strict licensing compliance: indices only ingest documentation with verified open licenses.

features.name: Thousands of Indexed Documents
features.category: Answers Grounded in Real Documentation
features.oneLine: Man pages, Arch Wiki, FreeBSD Handbook, Homebrew, and TLDR pages — all indexed locally.
features.whatItIs: The RAG corpus is built from 20+ specialized scrapers that acquire system administration documentation from diverse sources. Every document is verified, deduplicated, and indexed on disk. The full source list and licensing details are maintained in a dedicated data sources document.
features.howItWorks: Scrapers acquire content from man pages (Linux and macOS), Arch Wiki, Stack Exchange (Stack Overflow, Server Fault, Unix & Linux, Ask Different), FreeBSD Handbook, Homebrew formulae, TLDR pages, and vendor documentation. The index builder processes, chunks, and embeds each document for retrieval.
features.limitsAndInvariants: No scraping of paywalled or copyrighted content without explicit license verification.

features.name: Cite-and-Verify Links
features.category: Answers Grounded in Real Documentation
features.oneLine: Every suggested command cites the local on-disk manual page — no hallucinated flags.
features.whatItIs: When Halbert recommends a command or configuration directive, it cites the specific documentation source. You can open the referenced man page or wiki article yourself to verify the suggestion before running it.
features.howItWorks: RAG retrieval results include source metadata (document title, section, origin URL or man page reference). These citations are preserved through prompt injection and surfaced in the agent's response alongside the recommendation.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Citations reference the locally indexed copy, not external URLs — they work offline.

features.name: Web Search Fallback
features.category: Answers Grounded in Real Documentation
features.oneLine: When local knowledge is insufficient, the agent can search the web — off by default, explicit opt-in.
features.whatItIs: For queries that fall outside the local RAG corpus (new software, recent CVEs, niche hardware), the agent can perform a web search to supplement its local knowledge. This capability is disabled by default and requires explicit user opt-in.
features.howItWorks: The web search tool dispatches queries to search APIs and extracts relevant snippets. Results are injected into the agent's context alongside local RAG results, with clear attribution distinguishing local documentation from web sources.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Off by default. Cloud models and web search are switches that must be explicitly enabled — no telemetry, ever.

features.name: Unified Three-Panel Shell
features.category: A Workspace, Not Another Chat Window
features.oneLine: System domain rail, context stage, and agent conversation visible simultaneously — no modal context-switching.
features.whatItIs: The primary desktop workspace. A navigation rail on the left lets you browse system domains (Storage, Services, Network, GPU, etc.). The center stage shows the active domain's inventory and controls. The right panel holds the agent conversation. All three are visible simultaneously — you never lose context by switching tabs.
features.howItWorks: Built as a Tauri 2 desktop app wrapping a React SPA. Keyboard shortcuts (Cmd+D for domain rail, Cmd+J for conversation, Cmd+B for context stage) toggle panel focus. The conversation panel maintains contextual awareness of whichever domain page you're currently inspecting.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Responsive: on small screens, gracefully transitions from three side-by-side panels to stacked drawer views.

features.name: Inline Terminal Tiles with Sandbox
features.category: A Workspace, Not Another Chat Window
features.oneLine: Commands the agent runs stream live stdout/stderr directly inside chat turns, with sandbox isolation and redact filters.
features.whatItIs: When Halbert runs a shell command, it executes inside an inline terminal tile within the conversation turn — not in a hidden background process. You see live stdout/stderr, return codes, and can kill or re-run commands. The streaming subsystem provides sandbox isolation, PTY management, and automatic redaction of sensitive output.
features.howItWorks: Terminal output streams via WebSocket from the backend PTY session into xterm.js-backed inline tiles. The sandbox module isolates command execution. The redact filter scrubs sensitive patterns (API keys, passwords) from streamed output before it reaches the frontend.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Destructive commands require explicit user approval before execution.

features.name: Direct @Mentions for Hardware & Services
features.category: A Workspace, Not Another Chat Window
features.oneLine: Reference a live disk, service, or network interface directly in chat — the agent gets the full discovery context.
features.whatItIs: Type @ in a chat message to reference a specific discovered item — a disk volume, a running service, a network interface, a GPU. The agent receives the full discovery context for that item, so it can reason about its current state without you having to copy and paste system output.
features.howItWorks: The @mention system indexes all currently discovered items and presents an autocomplete dropdown. Selected items inject their full discovery record into the agent's turn context.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Only items from the most recent scanner run are available for mention — stale items are not surfaced.

features.name: Keyboard-First Command Palette
features.category: A Workspace, Not Another Chat Window
features.oneLine: Press / to open instant fuzzy search across every feature, domain, and setting.
features.whatItIs: A fast modal search that lets keyboard-oriented users jump to any dashboard page, setting, or discovered item without touching the mouse. Fuzzy matching means partial keywords work.
features.howItWorks: Indexes all navigation targets, settings labels, and discovered items. Opens on / keypress (when no input is focused), filters in real-time as you type, and navigates on selection.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Does not trigger when typing in input fields or text areas.

features.name: Shell Integration
features.category: A Workspace, Not Another Chat Window
features.oneLine: Injects Halbert helpers into .bashrc and .zshrc so the agent is available from any terminal session.
features.whatItIs: Halbert can inject helper functions and aliases into your shell configuration, making the agent accessible from any terminal session without opening the dashboard. This bridges the gap between the GUI workspace and the command line.
features.howItWorks: Shell integration modules generate configuration snippets for bash and zsh that register Halbert helper commands. These snippets are appended to the user's shell RC files on opt-in.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Shell modifications require explicit user opt-in — Halbert never modifies shell configuration files without permission.

features.name: Dynamic Skill Registry
features.category: A Workspace, Not Another Chat Window
features.oneLine: Agent loads and composes skill extensions at runtime — new capabilities without redeployment.
features.whatItIs: The skill system allows Halbert's capabilities to be extended through composable skill definitions. Skills are parsed, validated, and registered at runtime. The composer assembles skills into the agent's active tool set based on the current context and user configuration.
features.howItWorks: The skill registry discovers and loads skill definitions. The parser validates skill schemas. The composer resolves dependencies between skills and assembles the active skill set for each agent turn based on context (e.g., a home automation skill is only composed when HA is configured).
features.limitsAndInvariants: Skills cannot override core safety policies — the policy engine evaluates all tool calls regardless of their skill origin.

features.name: Olivetti Design Language
features.category: A Workspace, Not Another Chat Window
features.oneLine: Vermilion & Bone tokens, display serif typography, and a calm editorial aesthetic across the entire system.
features.whatItIs: Every surface in Halbert — dashboard, marketing site, feature reference, design system package — shares a unified visual identity inspired by Olivetti's mid-century industrial design. The Vermilion & Bone palette, display serif headings, and monospace technical text create a calm, intentional aesthetic.
features.howItWorks: Design tokens are defined once in shared-tokens/ and consumed by both Tailwind CSS v4 and the @halbert/design-system package. The design system ships plain CSS backed by these tokens — no Tailwind in library source — so it works under any CSS framework version.
features.limitsAndInvariants: The design system declares react ^18.2.0 || ^19.0.0 as a peer dependency, enabling a React 19 upgrade without republishing.

features.name: Instant Local Voice Pipeline
features.category: Speaks and Listens Without the Cloud
features.oneLine: On-device streaming ASR and TTS with sub-second latency, wake-word detection, barge-in, and speaker identification.
features.whatItIs: The entire speech pipeline runs locally on Sherpa-ONNX neural models. The system runs two concurrent tracks: a Speech Track (VAD → Wake Word Spotter → Streaming ASR → Speaker ID) and an Ambient Track (Energy Gate → Audio Tagger → Anomaly Detector). TTS with rapid barge-in support means Halbert stops speaking the instant you start.
features.howItWorks: Audio ingress adapters capture PCM from local microphones, Wyoming protocol satellites, RTSP streams, and WebRTC. Chunks feed into an async ring buffer. The speech track processes voice activity detection, wake word spotting, streaming transcription, and speaker identification in sequence. Results emit as VoiceTurnObservation events.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Push-to-talk by default: continuous ambient listening requires explicit owner opt-in. Gracefully degrades if sherpa-onnx is not installed.

features.name: Acoustic Environment Sensing
features.category: Speaks and Listens Without the Cloud
features.oneLine: Ambient sound monitoring that detects anomalies: fan bearing failures, alarms, sudden noise spikes.
features.whatItIs: The ambient track of the audio pipeline continuously monitors environmental sounds for anomalies. This goes beyond speech recognition — it detects physical events like fan bearing failures, smoke alarms, glass breaking, and sudden noise spikes that may indicate emergencies.
features.howItWorks: The ambient track runs an energy gate to filter silence, an audio tagger to classify sound events, and an anomaly detector to identify deviations from the learned ambient baseline. Detections emit as AcousticEventObservation events that feed into the findings system.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Audio is never recorded or stored — only event metadata (type, confidence, timestamp) is persisted.

features.name: Screenshot & Diagram Analysis
features.category: Speaks and Listens Without the Cloud
features.oneLine: Paste, drag, or capture an image for the vision model to analyze and explain — Wayland-aware screen capture included.
features.whatItIs: Image analysis via the vision model tier — paste, drag-and-drop, or screen-capture an image into a turn for the agent to analyze. The screen capture module works on both X11 and Wayland compositors, and on macOS via ScreenCaptureKit.
features.howItWorks: Images are routed to the vision model tier. The agent can describe, annotate, and reason about screenshots, architecture diagrams, error dialogs, and configuration UIs. The vision tools support multi-image analysis and region-of-interest cropping.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Images are processed locally by default — cloud vision endpoints require explicit configuration.

features.name: Visual Aura State Indicator
features.category: Speaks and Listens Without the Cloud
features.oneLine: A non-intrusive ambient pulse reflecting voice pipeline state: idle, listening, thinking, speaking.
features.whatItIs: The VoiceHUD presents a subtle visual indicator that reflects the current audio pipeline state. Instead of a blinking microphone icon, the aura provides ambient awareness of whether Halbert is idle, actively listening, processing speech, or speaking a response.
features.howItWorks: The AudioState enum (IDLE, LISTENING, RECOGNIZED, THINKING, SPEAKING, ERROR) is published via SSE to the frontend. The VoiceHUD component renders the corresponding aura animation. State transitions are smooth and non-jarring.
features.limitsAndInvariants: The aura never obscures content or demand attention — it sits at the periphery of the interface.

features.name: Zero-Friction Peer Pairing
features.category: One Mind Across Every Machine
features.oneLine: Secure 4-digit PIN handshake over mDNS or direct IP, with per-peer tokens and surgical revocation.
features.whatItIs: Link multiple machines running Halbert into a unified fleet. The satellite discovers the desktop via mDNS, requests pairing, and the desktop displays a 4-digit PIN. Once confirmed, both nodes exchange cryptographic tokens. For Tailscale networks (where mDNS doesn't cross), manual IP pairing works identically.
features.howItWorks: Step 1: Satellite POSTs to /api/peers/pair → Desktop returns a PIN. Step 2: User confirms. Step 3: Satellite sends PIN to /api/peers/verify → Desktop validates and returns a bearer token. Each satellite gets its own token. Revocation is surgical: DELETE /api/peers/{node_id}. Token rotation = revoke + re-pair. Federation also includes Wake-on-LAN for sleeping peers.
features.toolingAndBackend: routes/peers.py, federation/ (mDNS discovery, compute routing, WoL)
features.limitsAndInvariants: Unauthorized devices on the local network cannot execute remote commands — pairing requires physical confirmation.

features.name: Canonical Host + Satellite Bodies
features.category: One Mind Across Every Machine
features.oneLine: One primary memory store; satellite machines proxy tool execution and local sensors. Shared context, distributed hardware.
features.whatItIs: The 'One Mind, Many Bodies' architecture. A Canonical Host (e.g., an always-on Mac Studio or home server) acts as the primary memory store, conversation history, and identity. Satellite bodies (laptop, Raspberry Pi, etc.) proxy their local sensors and tool execution capabilities to the host.
features.howItWorks: The federation middleware routes requests between host and satellites. Satellites register their local capabilities (scanners, hardware, microphones) with the host. The host's agent can request tool execution on any paired satellite, and results return through the authenticated peer channel.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Memory is centralized on the Canonical Host — satellites do not maintain independent conversation history.

features.name: Remote Tool Execution Proxy
features.category: One Mind Across Every Machine
features.oneLine: Run tools on a peer machine from the primary dashboard — results return through the authenticated channel.
features.whatItIs: The peer tool proxy allows the agent on the Canonical Host to invoke MCP tools on any paired satellite. This enables scenarios like running GPU diagnostics on a remote workstation or checking sensor data on a Raspberry Pi — all from the primary dashboard.
features.howItWorks: The proxy routes MCP tool calls (tools/list, tools/call) to the paired peer's MCP server over HTTP JSON-RPC 2.0. Authentication uses the per-peer bearer token established during pairing. Results are returned to the host agent's turn context.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Remote tool calls are subject to the same approval policies as local calls — no privilege escalation through federation.

features.name: Built-in MCP Server
features.category: One Mind Across Every Machine
features.oneLine: Halbert exposes its own tools and resources for external agents to consume via the Model Context Protocol.
features.whatItIs: Halbert doesn't just consume MCP tools — it exposes its own capabilities as an MCP server. External agents (Claude, other Halbert instances, custom tooling) can discover and invoke Halbert's tools, access its discovered resources, and query its knowledge base through the standard MCP JSON-RPC interface.
features.howItWorks: The MCP server module implements the tools/list and tools/call endpoints, exposing Halbert's tool registry to external consumers. A camera gate module controls which vision-related resources are exposed based on privacy configuration.
features.limitsAndInvariants: The MCP server respects the same policy engine as internal tool calls — external agents cannot bypass permission boundaries.

features.name: Home Assistant Entity Control
features.category: A Home That Pays Attention
features.oneLine: Lights, climate, sensors, switches — direct local API integration, no vendor cloud, no subscription.
features.whatItIs: Halbert connects directly to a local Home Assistant instance, providing entity control, area mapping, and service calls without any vendor cloud dependency. An autonomy gate prevents unauthorized control of security-critical entities like locks and alarm systems.
features.howItWorks: The HA client syncs entity states via the Home Assistant WebSocket API. Dashboard routes expose status, entity listing, service calls, area mapping, and connection configuration. The agent's HA tool enables natural-language control ("turn off the living room lights") with the autonomy gate enforcing authorization for security entities.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Lock and security boundaries require explicit secondary confirmation — the agent cannot toggle locks or arm/disarm alarms without approval.

features.name: Autonomous Cognitive Loop
features.category: A Home That Pays Attention
features.oneLine: Perceive → Reason → Act → Observe → Reflect — runs on a configurable timer, only invokes the LLM when something novel happens.
features.whatItIs: The cognitive loop is the autonomous perception-reason-action tick that would run on a configurable interval (default 5-15 minutes). It gathers state from HA entities, Frigate events, scanner findings, the occupancy model, and behavior predictions. It uses cheap heuristics for routine checks and only invokes the LLM when something novel happens.
features.howItWorks: The loop runs in a background thread. PERCEIVE gathers state from all connected sources. REASON flushes pending events into the agent's cognition queue. ACT routes desired actions through the AutonomyGate. OBSERVE checks whether actions had the intended effect. REFLECT logs the decision chain to the orchestration timeline.
features.limitsAndInvariants: The loop is interruptible — if the user sends a chat message while the loop is running, the chat takes priority. The action generation logic is currently a scaffold awaiting full implementation.

features.name: Occupancy & Behavior Learning
features.category: A Home That Pays Attention
features.oneLine: Multi-signal presence correlation and pattern prediction — learns routines without explicit schedules.
features.whatItIs: The occupancy model correlates multiple presence signals — Frigate face detection, smart lock events, WiFi device presence, Bluetooth proximity — to determine who is home, where they are, and how confident the estimate is. The behavior inferrer learns recurring patterns from timeline history and predicts upcoming routines.
features.howItWorks: The OccupancyModel ingests PresenceSignal events with confidence weights and TTL decay. It maintains a PersonPresence record for each identified individual. The PatternInferrer scans the SQLite-backed timeline to learn time-of-day, day-of-week, device usage, and guest patterns, then predicts upcoming actions.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Occupancy data stays strictly local — no presence or behavior patterns are ever transmitted externally.

features.name: Frigate NVR Event Ingestion
features.category: A Home That Pays Attention
features.oneLine: Local object-detection events and snapshots from cameras, no cloud streaming.
features.whatItIs: Halbert ingests events from a local Frigate NVR installation — person detection, vehicle detection, pet detection — without streaming video to any cloud service. You get real-time awareness of what's happening on your property through local processing only.
features.howItWorks: The Frigate routes query the local Frigate instance for camera configurations, recent events and review segments, event snapshots, and latest frames. A vision authorization gate controls which camera feeds the agent can access based on privacy configuration.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Video never leaves the local network. The vision authorization gate prevents the agent from accessing cameras in sensitive areas unless explicitly permitted.
